evidence: The paper applies and analyzes GraphRAG on the FNS 2023 financial narrative summarization dataset, comparing it to naive RAG and proposing an optimized domain adaptation variant.
The paper proposes an LLM-as-optimizer framework that extends GraphRAG's domain adaptation strategy to improve entity and relation extraction prompts using ground-truth summaries.
Paper defines and operationalizes human-AI synergy as outperforming max(human, AI), reports pooled effect g=-0.23 across 370 effect sizes
Paper operationalizes human augmentation as outperforming human alone, reports pooled effect g=0.64 across 370 effect sizes; distinguishes from synergy
Paper presents a MAC framework for enterprise applications with hierarchical agents, inter-agent communication, payload referencing, and dynamic routing.
The paper's entire analysis is organized around human-AI collaboration as the central construct; it synthesizes 96 factors and three conceptual framings of this concept.
The paper's primary contribution is a multi-angled conceptualization and definition of Agentic AI, including capability comparison tables, autonomy levels, and an evolution narrative from GenAI.
Chain-of-thought reasoning is a central mechanism surveyed; the paper traces CoT from early prompting (Wei et al.) through its evolution into deep reasoning in Agentic AI systems.
RAG is extensively surveyed as the primary memory and knowledge-retrieval mechanism in Agentic AI, with coverage of classic RAG, adaptive RAG, experience-based RAG, and knowledge graph retrieval.
Proposes a novel three-dimensional levels-of-autonomy framework (flexibility, proactivity, supervision) for AI agents in knowledge work
The survey introduces and defines LLM-based multi-agent systems as a formal research area with a four-dimensional taxonomy.
The survey provides the first systematic taxonomy of agent communication paradigms (cooperative/debate/competitive), structures (layered/decentralized/centralized/shared pool), and content.
The survey systematically defines agent capability acquisition via feedback types (environment/agent/human/none) and adjustment strategies (memory/self-evolution/dynamic generation).
MetoFormer-HQ is an application for multivariate metocean forecasting using Korean coastal buoy data
MetoFormer-HQ applies and advances metocean forecasting with three new architectural components
Paper defines and operationalizes human-AI synergy as a formal concept analogous to strong synergy in human groups, using Hedges g vs max(human,AI) baseline
Paper formally defines human augmentation (human-AI > human alone) as a distinct weaker criterion from synergy, and reports pooled effect size g=0.64
Three-level meta-analytic model operationalizes and quantifies human-AI synergy concept across 370 effect sizes
The paper defines and formalizes information asymmetry in LLM-MAS as its central research problem, calling it the first work to study this from the individual-agent perspective.
The paper proposes iAgents (Informative Multi-Agent Systems) as a new MAS paradigm for information-asymmetric collaboration.
iAgents uses InfoNav as its core communication navigation mechanism; the paper derives the method from the problem of information-asymmetric MAS.
The paper introduces a systematic study and evaluation framework for community-specific content moderation using fine-tuned SLMs with subreddit-specific rules and context
The paper directly uses and evaluates community-specific content moderation as its primary task
MiniGPT-4 demonstrates that aligning a frozen visual encoder with a frozen LLM via a single linear projection sufficiently achieves vision-language alignment
MiniGPT-4 is a multimodal LLM that uses a frozen Vicuna LLM extended with visual input via projection alignment
MiniGPT-4 proposes a two-stage training approach: large-scale pretraining followed by curated fine-tuning on 3,500 high-quality image-description pairs
RAG is the core architecture of the system; the paper explicitly defines RAG as the mechanism for real-time information grounding and hallucination reduction via DART, ECOS, and Google News APIs.
The paper proposes and implements an explainable GPT-based stock investment analysis system as its primary contribution, directly introducing the concept of XAI applied to multi-source stock analysis
The system is built around RAG for real-time data retrieval as a core architectural component
AgentVerse proposes a general framework for multi-agent collaboration inspired by human group dynamics, introducing dynamic expert recruitment and structured collaborative decision-making.
AgentVerse documents emergent volunteer, conformity, and destructive behaviors in Minecraft multi-agent experiments — the first systematic analysis of such behaviors in LLM multi-agent systems.
QuantAgent is the first multi-agent LLM framework explicitly designed for high-frequency algorithmic trading, operating solely on OHLC price data
The paper introduces CoT prompting applied to financial news headline analysis for sector ETF allocation, proposing a two-stage structured reasoning pipeline as its core methodological contribution.
The framework's Task1 and Task2 prompts explicitly use CoT step-by-step reasoning to extract keywords, map sectors, and derive portfolio weights from news headlines.
The paper's core investigation is how human-in-the-loop AI services affect downstream consumer behavior in investment advisory
The entire system is built on RAG: FAISS-indexed dense retrieval feeds retrieved documents into LLM prompts for grounded financial Q&A generation

TradingAgents proposes the core architecture of specialized LLM agent roles (analyst, researcher, trader, risk manager) collaborating via structured communication for financial trading — instantiating the concept of LLM multi-agent financial trading.
The paper builds and evaluates a concrete instantiation of the LLM multi-agent financial trading concept using specialized roles and structured debate.
AgentVerse introduces the Expert Recruitment stage where a recruiter agent dynamically generates role descriptions to form an adaptive agent group based on goal and feedback.
Studies human-AI collaboration through a large-scale randomized field experiment; identifies three mechanisms reshaping teamwork
Empirically documents and extends the jagged frontier to field ad performance metrics (text quality→CTR, image quality→CPC)
First experimental documentation of diversity collapse in agentic human-AI teaming; traces mechanism to delegation behavior
Identifies and names the delegation workflow as the integrating behavioral mechanism underlying HAI productivity and quality effects
Paper defines and operationalizes Competitive/Adaptive/Strategic trading personas as the core contribution, embedding them via system-level prompt injection.
The paper is centrally about AI-augmented organizations and studies collaboration model limitations within them
ChatCollab introduces a configurable framework where humans and AI agents collaborate as peers with equal role-level standing in a software team

ChatCollab embeds human-AI collaborative teaming as its central design goal: humans and AI agents operate as equal peers sharing the same Slack channel and event timeline, adopting differentiated software team roles

The paper's central thesis is that motivation and accuracy information improve HAI performance by enabling well-calibrated trust; trust calibration is defined and operationalised as the core dependent construct throughout.
The paper discovers and characterizes the collaborative scaling law: performance follows logistic growth as agents scale, with emergence at ~100 agents
MacNet (Multi-Agent Collaboration Network) is the central contribution of this paper, organizing LLM agents into DAG topologies
Paper explicitly frames MAS topology as an underexplored, learnable property and proposes a structured research agenda around it
The entire paper is built around optimizing MAS topology through the three-stage framework
The paper coins 'agentic trading' as the paradigm of mapping AT pipeline components to agent pools with DAG orchestration.
The entire framework is built around the agentic trading paradigm.
Digital Fragmented Knowledge is the central contribution of the GenAI SECI model — partial field knowledge in cyberspace leveraged via GenAI without full formalization
The internalization stage relies on human-AI collaborative workshops for symbol grounding; GenAI recommends fragments to stimulate reflective observation among participants
Both address GenAI augmentation of knowledge work; this paper focuses on tacit knowledge capture while the other surveys broader explicit knowledge workflows in finance

Paper formulates a three-layer (short/middle/long-term) memory with per-layer decay constants and retrieval thresholds, replacing Park et al.'s single blended recency/relevancy/importance score with per-layer scoring (Section 4.1).
TradingGPT is itself a multi-agent LLM system with specialized character-based trading agents that collaborate via debate to produce trading decisions, an instance of this concept's general pattern.

Agents are assigned discrete risk-preference characters (risk-seeking/neutral/averse) plus an industry subscope via prompt injection, enriching memory diversity and decision robustness (paper's second headline contribution).

TradingAgents' related work explicitly groups TradingGPT among 'Debate-driven agents ... enhance reasoning and factual validity by employing LLM debates among agents with different roles, improving sentiment classification and increasing robustness in trading decisions' (sections/2.related.tex).

FinCon extends the LLM multi-agent trading concept beyond single-stock trading to multi-asset portfolio management via mean-variance optimization, and adds a formal dual-level (within-episode CVaR + over-episode CVRF) risk-control mechanism absent from prior instances of this concept.

The paper explicitly proposes, names, and formalizes Conceptual Verbal Reinforcement (CVRF) as its core over-episode risk-control contribution, contrasting it with prior textual-gradient-descent and verbal-reinforcement approaches (Section 3.1.2, Algorithm 1).

HedgeAgents extends the LLM multi-agent trading concept with cross-asset-class hedging (Bitcoin, stocks, forex simultaneously) coordinated through three distinct conference types, rather than a single-asset-class or single-decision-channel design used by prior work in this concept's key_papers.

The paper explicitly proposes and names the fund-manager/hedging-expert architecture coordinated via three conference types (Budget Allocation, Experience Sharing, Extreme Market), formalizing 'hedging' as an explicit multi-agent coordination pattern (Section 3.2-3.4).

CryptoMAS extends the LLM multi-agent trading concept to cryptocurrency portfolio management with a fixed three-modality agent split (Crypto/News/Trading) and treats MAS communication architecture (hierarchical/collaborative/debate) and per-agent capability (zero-shot/CoT/RAG/skill) as two independently-crossed design axes benchmarked in one framework across three LLM backbones, a systematic evaluation not present in prior instances of this concept.

The paper systematically evaluates three existing communication structures (hierarchical, collaborative/cooperative refinement, adversarial debate) as an explicit swappable design axis governing how the Crypto Agent and News Agent reach the Trading Agent, without introducing a new structure type.

RAG is one of four capability configurations: the Crypto Agent retrieves the top-3 cosine-similar historical market weeks (via an 11-dim engineered feature vector) as outcome-labelled analogues injected into its prompt, a standard dense-retrieval RAG application rather than an extension of the RAG mechanism itself.

CoT is one of four capability configurations: agents emit an explicit <reasoning> block before their structured JSON output, a standard application of chain-of-thought prompting rather than a modification of the technique.

Paper explicitly proposes injecting LLM-derived news recommendation and risk-assessment scores as action-channel and CVaR-objective-channel perturbations of a single-agent RL trading policy (Sections 5.3-5.4), naming it as the paper's main contribution.

Related Work explicitly contrasts the two: 'Other hybrid RL-LLM approaches include FinCon, which makes a complex distillation of information through a synthesized multi-agent collaboration mechanism. In this paper, we only use simple prompts.' Both attack hybrid RL/LLM-informed risk-aware financial decision-making from different angles.

QuantAgents cites HedgeAgents (li2025hedgeagents) as its strongest baseline and explicitly reports surpassing it by 19.15% ARR / 30.02% TR / 29.05% SR in Table 1; both papers share the same author lineage (Xiangyu Li, Yawen Zeng, Xiaofen Xing, Jin Xu, Xiangmin Xu) and a near-identical four-agent fund-company framing (Otto/Bob/Dave/Emily roles), indicating QuantAgents is a direct architectural follow-up to HedgeAgents.

The paper's stated core contribution is 'a multi-agent financial system that incorporates simulated trading' with 'a dual reward mechanism to coordinate agent behaviors, i.e., rewards from the real market and rewards from simulated trading,' formalized via adaptive sigmoid-weighted mixing of w_t^sim and w_t^real in Section 3.4.

QuantAgents decomposes fund management into four specialized LLM agents (manager, simulated-trading analyst, risk-control analyst, market-news analyst) that coordinate via structured meetings to produce trading decisions, directly instantiating the multi-agent financial trading pattern.

FLAG-Trader partially fine-tunes an LLM's own parameters to serve directly as the actor-critic policy/value network of a PPO-trained trading agent, a design the paper explicitly contrasts with prompted multi-agent LLM frameworks.

FLAG-Trader's related work explicitly cites FinCon as an example of the costly multi-agent 'agentic framework' approach it positions itself as a training-based alternative to, on the same LLM-for-trading-decisions problem.
FLAG-Trader's related work cites TradingGPT alongside FinCon as a hybrid LLM-agentic trading system contrasted with its own single fused LLM-RL design, on the same LLM-for-trading-decisions problem.
AMA deploys the TradingAgents multi-agent debate architecture verbatim as its 'TradeAgent' baseline, running it live across five LLM backbones under AMA's standardized protocol.

AMA deploys four pre-existing LLM multi-agent trading architectures (InvestorAgent, TradeAgent/TradingAgents, HedgeFundAgent, DeepFundAgent) as benchmark participants without introducing a new multi-agent architecture itself.

Paper explicitly proposes Agent Market Arena as 'the first lifelong, real-time, and multi-class-asset evaluation framework for LLM-based trading agents,' defining the live multi-market benchmark methodology as its central contribution.

TradingGroup extends the LLM multi-agent trading concept with a fixed (non-debate) five-agent pipeline whose forecasting, style, and decision agents each self-reflect on their own reward-labeled case history pulled from a shared data-synthesis pipeline, and where that same reward-labeled log doubles as filtered SFT data for post-training the base LLM -- a data-substrate design not present in prior instances of this concept.

The paper explicitly proposes a self-reflection mechanism, integrated into the Stock-Forecasting, Style-Preference, and Trading-Decision agents, that extracts each agent's own recent successful/failed cases from the data-synthesis pipeline's reward-labeled log and injects a distilled experience summary into the next prompt.

"Building on the proven strengths of reflection modules (FinAgent) and MAS architectures (TradingAgents), TradingGroup integrates self-reflection into its trading-decision, price-forecasting, and style-preference agents, and couples them with a dynamic risk-management module, achieving higher stability and backtesting performance."

Paper explicitly introduces StockSim's core contribution as two complementary simulation modes -- order-level LOB execution and candlestick-level execution -- unified behind a single interface, presented as the central architectural novelty distinguishing it from prior single-mode simulators.

StockSim's LLMTradingAgent delegates decision-making to a team of specialist LLMs (market-technical, news, fundamental analysts) coordinated by an aggregator, supporting multi-agent LLM trading configurations as an evaluation target rather than proposing a new coordination architecture itself.

"frameworks designed for multi-agent LLM coordination, such as TradingAgents, often use highly simplified market representations based solely on coarse historical data, omitting realistic execution and latency considerations critical for evaluating LLM behavior."
